title: Introducing the Metrics API for Mastra Platform
summary: Query cost, latency, and errors by agent, thread, or time.
body_markdown:
You can now query token usage, model cost, latency, and error rates with Mastra platform's[Metrics API](https://mastra.ai/docs/mastra-platform/api#metrics-api) . Use the Mastra Client SDK, Mastra CLI, or observability endpoints to get totals, breakdowns, time series, and percentile data from production Mastra projects.


[Traces](https://mastra.ai/docs/studio/observability#traces) show what happened in a single run, while[metrics](https://mastra.ai/docs/observability/metrics/overview) aggregate across every run. This lets you see which model, conversation, or tool calls cost the most, run the slowest, or fail most often. You can combine query types with time ranges and status filters to surface important insights to share with your team.


Your browser does not support the video tag.


We[launched metrics](https://mastra.ai/blog/introducing-studio-metrics) earlier this year, letting you view model costs, latency, and error counts in Mastra platform and Studio. Today, using the Metrics API, you can construct your own queries to generate custom reports, build dashboards, send data to downstream services, or post alerts to connected chat platforms when model costs or error rates rise.


You can combine the Metrics API with[code mode](https://mastra.ai/docs/agents/code-mode) to build agents capable of constructing their own queries on the fly to answer questions, summarize insights, or generate PDFs for team members and stakeholders.


## Get started


Metric queries need a platform access token and your project ID, sent with each request. Use the correct Mastra observability[base URL](https://mastra.ai/docs/mastra-platform/api#metrics-api) for your project's region:


- **US** :` https://observability.mastra.ai`
- **EU** :` https://observability.eu.mastra.ai`


Each example below asks for total token usage and estimated cost for the last 30 days. The` timestamp` filter is optional. If` start` and` end` are omitted, queries return all available data.


### Mastra Client SDK


Use the analytics methods with Mastra[Client SDK](https://mastra.ai/reference/observability/metrics/queries#client-sdk) :


Terminal


```text
npm   install   @mastra/client-js@latest
```


note


Requires` @mastra/client-js@1.9.0` or later, added in[PR #14270](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/14270) .


src/metrics.ts


```text
import   {   MastraClient   }   from   "  @mastra/client-js  "  ;


const   mastraClient   =   new   MastraClient  ({
baseUrl:   "  https://observability.mastra.ai  "  ,
headers: {
Authorization:   `  Bearer   ${  process.env.MASTRA_PLATFORM_ACCESS_TOKEN  }`  ,
"  X-Mastra-Project-Id  "  : process.env.MASTRA_PROJECT_ID  !
}
});


await   mastraClient.  getMetricAggregate  ({
name: [  "  mastra_model_total_input_tokens  "  ,   "  mastra_model_total_output_tokens  "  ],
aggregation:   "  sum  "  ,
filters: {
timestamp: {
start:   new   Date  (  "  2026-09-13T00:00:00Z  "  ),
end:   new   Date  (  "  2026-10-13T00:00:00Z  "  )
}
},
comparePeriod:   "  previous_period  "
});
```


### Mastra CLI


Install or upgrade the Mastra CLI globally:


Terminal


```text
npm   install   -g   mastra@latest
```


note


Requires` mastra@1.9.2` or later, added in[PR #16563](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/16563) .


Run the[mastra api metric](https://mastra.ai/reference/cli/mastra#mastra-api-metric-aggregate) commands from your terminal. The CLI reads` MASTRA_PLATFORM_ACCESS_TOKEN` and` MASTRA_PROJECT_ID` from your environment:


Terminal


```text
mastra   api   --url   https://observability.mastra.ai   metric   aggregate   '  {"name":["mastra_model_total_input_tokens","mastra_model_total_output_tokens"],"aggregation":"sum","filters":{"timestamp":{"start":"2026-09-13T00:00:00Z","end":"2026-10-13T00:00:00Z"}},"comparePeriod":"previous_period"}  '
```


### Observability endpoints


Send a` POST` request to one of the[Metrics API endpoints](https://mastra.ai/docs/mastra-platform/api#endpoints-1) . Include the` MASTRA_PLATFORM_ACCESS_TOKEN` and` MASTRA_PROJECT_ID` variables in the request:


Terminal


```text
curl   -X   POST   "  https://observability.mastra.ai/api/observability/metrics/aggregate  "   \
-H   "  Authorization: Bearer   $MASTRA_PLATFORM_ACCESS_TOKEN"   \
-H   "  X-Mastra-Project-Id:   $MASTRA_PROJECT_ID"   \
-H   "  Content-Type: application/json  "   \
-d   '  {
"name": ["mastra_model_total_input_tokens", "mastra_model_total_output_tokens"],
"aggregation": "sum",
"filters": { "timestamp": { "start": "2026-09-13T00:00:00Z", "end": "2026-10-13T00:00:00Z" } },
"comparePeriod": "previous_period"
}  '
```


### Example Response


All requests are returned as JSON:


```text
{
"  value  "  :   6332830  ,
"  estimatedCost  "  :   14.66  ,
"  costUnit  "  :   "  USD  "  ,
"  previousValue  "  :   866647  ,
"  previousEstimatedCost  "  :   null  ,
"  changePercent  "  :   630.7  ,
"  costChangePercent  "  :   null
}
```


## Example queries


The following examples show how to query cost by token type, the most expensive conversations, daily token usage, latency percentiles, and failed runs. Each example uses the Mastra Client SDK, but the same queries work with the Mastra CLI and observability endpoints.


### Cost by token type


Query each token type on its own to see what drives cost. Cache writes, cache reads, and output tokens are priced differently:


```text
const   cacheWrites   =   await   mastraClient.  getMetricAggregate  ({
name: [  "  mastra_model_input_cache_write_tokens  "  ],
aggregation:   "  sum  "
// ...
});
```


### Cost by conversation


Group token usage by` threadId` to rank conversations by cost:


```text
const   conversations   =   await   mastraClient.  getMetricBreakdown  ({
groupBy: [  "  threadId  "  ],
aggregation:   "  sum  "
// ...
});
```


The same call with` groupBy: \["model"\]` gives cost by model, and` groupBy: \["rootEntityName"\]` gives cost by the agent or workflow.


### Tokens per day


Get token usage for each day:


```text
const   daily   =   await   mastraClient.  getMetricTimeSeries  ({
interval:   "  1d  "  ,
aggregation:   "  sum  "
// ...
});
```


### Latency percentiles


Get p50 and p95 agent run durations for each day:


```text
const   latency   =   await   mastraClient.  getMetricPercentiles  ({
name:   "  mastra_agent_duration_ms  "  ,
percentiles: [  0.5  ,   0.95  ],
interval:   "  1d  "
// ...
});
```


### Failed runs


Filter duration metrics by their` status` label to count failed runs:


```text
const   failedRuns   =   await   mastraClient.  getMetricAggregate  ({
name: [  "  mastra_agent_duration_ms  "  ],
aggregation:   "  count  "  ,
filters: {
labels: { status:   "  error  "   }
}
});
```
